 ET Online School Holiday Update Schools in several parts of India are observing holidays in the first week of November due to Diwali vacations, local elections and adverse weather conditions. With November 5 falling on Thursday, students and parents are keen to know whether schools will remain closed tomorrow. Andhra Pradesh has already announced a two-day holiday on November 4 and 5 in view of the upcoming Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections. Meanwhile, heavy rainfall warnings across parts of southern and eastern India could also lead to local school closure announcements, depending on weather conditions and instructions issued by district administrations.
 Andhra Pradesh schools closed on November 5 for MPTC, ZPTC elections
Andhra Pradesh will observe a holiday on November 5 for the MPTC and ZPTC elections. The two-day closure, covering educational institutions included in the election-related order, was announced to facilitate polling arrangements. Voting will take place on November 5, while counting of votes is scheduled for November 7. Students should check with their respective schools whether their institutions are covered by the order.

 Diwali school holidays 2026: Check state-wise vacation dates
Several states are observing extended Diwali vacations in November, although the schedules vary depending on local education department calendars and school categories. Here are some of the reported vacation schedules:
 Maharashtra: Several schools have Diwali vacations during November. BMC primary schools in Mumbai are scheduled to remain closed from November 5 to 23, while Pune's revised schedule provides a break from November 5 to 18.
 Goa: Schools are observing Diwali vacations from November 2 to 21.
 Gujarat: A 21-day Diwali vacation is scheduled from November 5 to 25.
 Bihar: Government and government-aided schools have a festival break from November 7 to 17.
 Chhattisgarh: Diwali holidays are scheduled from November 6 to 11.
 Rajasthan: Schools may observe an extended Diwali break from November 4 to 15.
 These dates may differ for private schools, government institutions and different education boards.
 Live Events
 IMD weather alert: Will heavy rainfall lead to school closures?
Weather conditions could also affect school operations in some regions. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued rainfall warnings for several parts of southern and eastern India following the passage of Cyclone Murasu. For November 4, heavy to very heavy rainfall was forecast at isolated places in north Coastal Andhra Pradesh and east Telangana. Heavy rainfall was also likely at isolated places in south Odisha, south Chhattisgarh and north Tamil Nadu.
 The IMD's subsequent forecast indicates that isolated heavy rainfall could continue over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal from November 5. Rainfall activity is also expected in parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. However, these weather warnings do not automatically mean schools will remain closed. District administrations will take decisions depending on local conditions and safety concerns.
 School holiday tomorrow: What should students and parents check?
Apart from Andhra Pradesh's election-related holiday and schools already observing Diwali vacations, no nationwide school closure has been announced for November 5. Weather-related holidays, if required, are likely to depend on district-level orders.
Students and parents should check notifications from their respective school administrations, district collectors and state education departments before travelling to school. Schools may also announce local closures if heavy rainfall, waterlogging or unsafe road conditions disrupt normal activities.
